suppressions.reason: Native-development TLS material, the same class as TRIVY-003 and TRIVY-004 but for the non-container paths. `make dev` and `make backend` set CB_DATA_DIR to apps/backend/.dev-data, and scripts/dev-tls.sh generates a self-signed EC certificate under its tls/ for the agent front door. Gitignored (.dev-data/), regenerated on demand, never source and never in a packaged RC artifact. Its absence made `make verify` fail its own security gate on every machine that had run the dev stack.
suppressions.compensating_control: tests/build/test_secret_suppression_scope.py asserts this path is gitignored and holds no git-tracked file, so the suppression cannot mask a committed key; scripts/secret_exposure_guard.sh blocks TLS material tracked in HEAD; Gitleaks still scans git history.

suppressions.reason: The repository-root data directory. The Makefile's default CB_DATA_DIR (?= ./circuitbreaker-data) and docker-compose.yml both resolve here, so a compose run or a dev-tls invocation that does not override CB_DATA_DIR writes its self-signed EC certificate to this tls/. Gitignored (circuitbreaker-data/) and ephemeral. Registered alongside TRIVY-007 rather than after it turns someone's gate red.
suppressions.compensating_control: Identical to TRIVY-007: the suppression-scope test proves the path is gitignored and untracked, secret_exposure_guard.sh blocks tracked TLS material in HEAD, and Gitleaks covers history.

suppressions.reason: Deliberately fake credentials in security documentation and isolated test fixtures exist to demonstrate and exercise detection; the paths are enumerated individually rather than by wildcard.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist names exact files, so a real secret in any other path still fails the gate; fixture values are asserted fake by the tests that consume them.

suppressions.reason: `cb config validate` passes min_length=_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH to validate_secret_value; generic-api-key reads the keyword argument next to a `secret`/`key` label as the credential. The matched text is a module-private constant name, not a value.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist matches on the constant's name rather than on a path, so every other line of cli.py — including the ones either side of these calls — is still scanned, and a real secret there fails the gate.

suppressions.reason: GET /agents/server-key/status returns current_key_fingerprint and successor_key_fingerprint — SHA digests of the agent server's public key, rendered on the Agents page and quoted verbatim in the frontend test fixture and the slice spec. A 32-character hex value beside a field name containing `key` is what generic-api-key matches; a digest of a public key is not a credential and discloses nothing that the admin API does not already return.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist matches the field name on the finding's line rather than allowlisting the two files, so every other line of those files is still scanned and a real secret in them fails the gate.

suppressions.reason: redactSensitive() strips PEM blocks, so apps/frontend/src/__tests__/agent-errors.test.js must hold a string of PEM shape to prove it does. The body is the 12 characters MIIBVgIBADAN, which decode to the 9 bytes 30 82 01 56 02 01 00 30 0d — a truncated PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo header (SEQUENCE, version INTEGER 0, and the start of the AlgorithmIdentifier) carrying no key material and no private exponent. The literal is written inline in the assertion that redaction removed it.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist matches that body on the finding's line rather than allowlisting the file, so every other line of the redaction corpus is still scanned and a real private key in the same file fails the gate.

suppressions.reason: dGVzdC12YXVsdC1rZXk= is base64 for the ASCII string "test-vault-key". tests/build/test_restore_dump_errors.py writes it into a stub snapshot so restore.sh can be asserted to carry CB_VAULT_KEY through into the restored env file; nothing is ever encrypted or decrypted with it. This is the same fabricated value already excused for apps/backend/tests/services/test_restore_targets.py by the documented-and-test-fixtures allowlist.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist matches the literal rather than a path, so a real vault key in any of the restore tests still fails the gate, and the next test asserting the same round-trip is covered without widening the suppression to another directory.

suppressions.reason: The design tool rewrites .superdesign/resume.json on every session, mapping each source file it read to the SHA-256 of that file's contents. generic-api-key reads a quoted 64-hex value beside a quoted label as a credential, so a session that touched only CSS turned the gate red on state holding no secret. A digest of a tracked source file discloses nothing: anyone who can read the manifest can read the file and recompute it.
suppressions.compensating_control: The allowlist matches the manifest's line shape -- a quoted source path with a file extension, a colon, a quoted 64-hex digest -- rather than allowlisting the path. A path entry would have been strictly worse than it looks: gitleaks drops a path-allowlisted file before applying any rule, so it would have silently stopped the cbe_ enrollment-token rule from firing inside that file. Verified against gitleaks 8.30.1 that a token planted in resume.json is still found under this entry, and that the same digest written as CB_VAULT_KEY = "<hex>" is still a finding. tests/build/test_superdesign_hash_manifest_allowlist.py fails if a paths key ever returns, if regexTarget stops being "line", or if the regex starts matching a credential assignment.
